extracted.Paper Title: Are alcoholism treatments effective? The Project MATCH data
extracted.Intervention: Outpatient psychosocial therapy (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy [CBT], Motivational Enhancement Therapy [MET], and Twelve Step Facilitation [TSF]) / Full treatment (attending all scheduled sessions)
extracted.Comparator: Zero treatment dropout group (participants who received no therapy sessions) and one session treatment group (participants who dropped out after one session)
extracted.Outcome: A median of only 3% of drinking outcome variance at follow-up could be attributed to treatment quantity. The zero treatment dropout group achieved a mean of 72 percent days abstinent at follow-up, duplicating two-thirds to three-fourths of the improvement seen in the full treatment group. Nearly all improvement occurred by week one before most therapy was delivered. Outcomes for the one session group were worse than for the zero session group, indicating a self-selection effect.
extracted.Effect Direction: Ineffective / Minimal effect (current psychosocial treatments for alcoholism are not particularly effective; most observed improvement is not attributable to treatment but to selection effects and non-treatment factors)

gold.gold_outcome: Drinks per drinking day||Percent days of abstinence

extracted.Intervention: A 6-week, twice-weekly supervised high-intensity exercise program consisting of 1-hour sessions (at ≥ 60% HR max) focused on weight-bearing exercises for postural control, endurance, and lower extremity strength, accompanied by daily home exercises.
extracted.Comparator: A non-intervention control group advised not to make lifestyle changes, meeting with a physical therapist for one hour at baseline, 6 weeks, and 6 months.
extracted.Outcome: No significant differences were found between the exercise and control groups regarding pain, other symptoms, or function (ADL and sport/recreation) measured by KOOS subscales at 6 weeks or 6 months. extracted.Effect Direction: No effect on pain or physical function; positive effect (improvement) on knee-related quality of life and mental health aspects.

extracted.Paper Title: Postoperative pain scores and analgesic requirements after thyroid surgery: Comparison of three intraoperative opioid regimens
extracted.Comparator: Intraoperative fentanyl-based regimen and sufentanil-based regimen
extracted.Outcome: Initial postoperative pain scores (VAS) were significantly higher in the remifentanil group (78±12) compared to the fentanyl (55±15) and sufentanil (60±10) groups (P < 0.05).
